taxonomyNote: NatureServe (following Crother 2017) restricts C. viridis to the prairie forms; the western forms are C. oreganus. Animal Diversity Web still treats oreganus as a C. viridis subspecies.
fieldMarks: 45-165 cm; light brown to black with a yellow head stripe (per Animal Diversity Web)
Horny rattle on the tail tip
Cryptic belly pattern in tan, yellow and gray
behavior: Mostly diurnal in cool weather, active in the evening and at night in hot weather
Active about late March/April to October/November
Migrates up to about 11 km between winter den and summer range and shows den fidelity
Eats mainly small mammals; juveniles in some regions mostly lizards
habitat: Prairies, arid basins and wooded mountains; uses mammal burrows, crevices and caves when inactive.
range: Southern Alberta and southern Saskatchewan south to northern Mexico, west to Idaho, Wyoming, Colorado and extreme eastern Arizona, east to the Dakotas, Nebraska, Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas.

lookalikes.name: Western rattlesnake
lookalikes.howToTell: Formerly grouped with C. viridis; ranges from southern British Columbia to Baja California and east to the Rockies.
